findings.statement: Broadcom’s AI accelerator business is built around six core hyperscale customers, including Google, Anthropic, OpenAI, Meta, and two additional partners such as AWS or Apple/ByteDance, as described in its customer‑list disclosures.
Broadcom projected fiscal year 2026 revenue of $104.7 billion, as reported in a company analysis.
Intel Corp: Intel disclosed that its Gaudi AI accelerator portfolio failed to meet an internal revenue target of $500 million, indicating that actual annual revenue from Gaudi was below that amount.

Intel Corp: Intel announced the Gaudi 3 AI accelerator in April 2024, stated OEM availability in Q2 2024, and formally launched the product on 24 September 2024, showing a release cadence of announcement → OEM availability → launch within a single quarter.
Broadcom’s VMware‑based subscription licenses are listed at $200–$400 per core per year for VCF and $100–$200 per core per year for VVF, representing the typical mid‑market tier pricing.

# Intel Fails To Achieve Gaudi AI “$500 Million” Revenue Target, Showing Slacking Performance In The AI Segment

[Muhammad Zuhair](https://wccftech.com/author/zuhairhaider/) •

[Comments](#comments "View comments")   [![](https://www.gstatic.com/images/branding/productlogos/googleg_gradient/v1/24px.svg) Add to Preferres Sources](javascript:void(0))

[![Intel's Gaudi 3 AI accelerator](https://cdn.wccftech.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/06/Intel-Gaudi-3-AI-accelerator_Black-Purple-Custom-728x486.png)](https://cdn.wccftech.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/06/Intel-Gaudi-3-AI-accelerator_Black-Purple-Custom.png)

Image Credits: Intel

Intel's Gaudi AI accelerators haven't managed to hit its "modest" quarterly revenue, as Team Blue fails in attracting market interest.

## Intel Misses Out On "Safe" Revenue Target For Gaudi AI Accelerators, Posing Questions On The Firm's Strategy

Team Blue's business in pretty much all segments, whether it is in the x86 markets or even the AI industry, isn't going too well since competitors have ramped up their solutions, giving Intel little to no chance of creating a clientele based similar to the likes of NVIDIA and AMD. In the recent Q3 2024 earnings, Intel's CEO Pat Gelsinger revealed (via [The Verge](https://www.theverge.com/2024/10/31/24284860/intel-gaudi-wont-meet-500-million-goal)) that the firm's Gaudi AI portfolio hasn't managed to meet revenue expectations at $500 million, which is indeed shocking, given that competitors like NVIDIA are eying towards a multi-billion dollar target.

[##### **Related Story** Intel Core Ultra 9 4995HX to Be the Fastest Nova Lake CPU for Laptops, Packing 28 Cores While Core Ultra 9 4970H Sticks With 16 CPU Cores & 12 iGPU Cores](https://wccftech.com/intel-core-ultra-9-4995hx-fastest-nova-lake-cpu-for-laptops-packing-28-cores/)

Intel's Pat Gelsinger claims that despite the launch of their newest Gaudi 3 AI accelerator, the firm has been unable to bring in business, mainly since the transition towards the newer platform has been quite slow, and the Gaudi 3 AI solution hasn't impressed customers to the extent that it leads to higher adoption rates. However, Intel remains confident with Gaudi, claiming that the market is in need of more cost-effective solutions that focus on an open-source environment.

![Intel Says It Won't Compete With NVIDIA In AI Market, Shifts Focus Towards Bringing Cost-Effective AI Solutions With Gaudi 3 1](https://cdn.wccftech.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/12/Intel-AIEverywhere-Event-5-scaled.jpg)

Pat Gelsinger (right), Intel chief executive officer, and Christoph Schell, executive vice president and chief commercial officer, display for the first time a next-generation Intel Gaudi 3 AI accelerator for deep learning and large-scale generative AI models, arriving on schedule next year, at Intel’s “AI Everywhere” event on Thursday, Dec. 14, 2023, in New York City. (Credit: Intel Corporation)

For those unaware, Intel has [reported $13.284 billion in non-GAAP revenue](https://wccftech.com/intel-q3-2024-earnings-dcai-saves-the-day/), which has actually beaten out the general consensus, but the fallback in reaching the $500 million mark with Gaudi has questioned Intel's approach towards the AI markets. The firm is more focused towards catering to cost-efficient workloads, which is why the Gaudi 3 doesn't compete in raw performance with the likes of NVIDIA's Blackwell and AMD's MI300X solutions. Until now, Intel has yet to tap into the "high-end" segment of the AI markets, and considering the presence of competitors, it seems like Intel needs to make a huge impact.

![](https://cdn.wccftech.com/files/placeholder-desktop.png)
